channel.title: web3ashley journal
channel.description: Notes on what actually loses businesses customers online.

item.title: Why your website is slow on a phone, and what it is costing you
item.description: Your site loads fine on your laptop and takes eleven seconds on a customer's phone. Here is where those seconds actually go, and which ones are worth buying back.

item.title: Your menu is a photograph, and Google cannot read a word of it
item.description: A menu saved as a JPEG or PDF is invisible to search, unreadable on a phone, and impossible for a screen reader. Here is what it costs and how to fix it in an afternoon.

item.title: Your contact form works. The notifications stopped six months ago.
item.description: The form submits, the thank-you page appears, and nothing arrives. It is the most expensive silent failure on a small business website. Here is how to test yours in five minutes.

item.title: How much should a website cost, and why the quotes vary so wildly
item.description: The same brief comes back at £500 and at £25,000. Both are real prices for genuinely different things. Here is what actually drives the number, so you can read a quote properly.

item.title: Do I need a website if I already have Instagram?
item.description: Social accounts do things a website cannot, and a website does things no social account can. The question is which risks you can live with. An honest answer, including when the answer is no.

item.title: What the delivery apps actually cost you, per order
item.description: The commission is the visible part. The customer relationship, the data, and the pricing pressure are the rest. Working out whether direct ordering is worth building.

item.title: The four numbers worth watching, and everything you can ignore
item.description: Analytics dashboards show you hundreds of metrics, and almost all of them are noise for a small business. Here are the four that change decisions.

item.title: Rebuild or repair? A test that takes ten minutes
item.description: Rebuilding a site that only needed fixing wastes money. Patching one that is structurally finished wastes more. Six questions that settle which situation you are in.

item.title: The free hour that beats most of what you can buy
item.description: For a local business, a properly filled Google Business Profile usually outperforms the website itself. It takes an hour, costs nothing, and most listings are half empty.

item.title: The spreadsheet that runs your business, and the day it goes missing
item.description: One file, one person who understands it, and no version of the business that survives losing either. How to tell when a spreadsheet has outgrown itself, and what to do about it.

item.title: Find out who actually owns your website, before you need to know
item.description: Domain, code, hosting and content can all sit in someone else's account without you realising. Four checks, twenty minutes, and the fix if the answer is wrong.
